answers.asked: How coherent was it, from 1 to 5?
Did you notice any flowery language, where simpler words would have been better?
Was there any flowery language left in this story, or none at all?
answers.answer: I would say none at all.

answers.asked: Did any character appear without enough introduction, description or back-story?
answers.answer: No. Although once again there was no physical description of characters (besides the split nail). That is a minor criticism though.

answers.asked: Did any character know something they shouldn't have known?
answers.answer: No, I don't remember that happening.

answers.asked: Did anything happen unrealistically quickly or slowly, or did the timing feel wrong anywhere?
answers.answer: I thought the pacing was good.

answers.asked: Did any event take an impossible or unlikely amount of time, like the food going sour after four minutes?
Which would you like: stop, adjust or compare?
answers.answer: I would say this story is significantly better than the previous stories I have read. I enjoyed the story and found it emotionally engaging, even though I had seen similar stories before in the course of doing this project. I don't think we need to do additional runs to prove the concept is viable as it clearly works right now.

decision.outcome: stop testing; no blind comparison and no further proof runs
decision.basis: The owner's judgement that the concept is viable, from reading this one story.
decision.not_established: No blind comparison against outline-only stories was run. This is not a gate result and does not reopen G1.
